about: The codebase index: one JSON record per source file, mapping vanilla 1.7.10 (oracle/src) to the native C engine (csrc/) and back, with what is left to port. Records live at index/<kind>/<source path with / kept>.json, e.g. index/java/entity/passive/EntityPig.java.json, index/csrc/engine/animals.c.json. tools/index_check.c (out/native/index_check) validates them; index/summary.json is built from them.

classes: every top-level and nested class, interface and enum declared in the file
java.side: server | client | common (runs on both, e.g. Entity, World, Block)
java.category: one of: world, worldgen, chunk, block, tileentity, item, crafting, inventory, entity, ai, pathfinding, player, combat, network, nbt, server, client_render, client_model, client_gui, client_audio, client_resources, client_input, particles, stats, commands, util, math, other
java.role: one or two sentences: what this file is in the game, in plain words
java.scope: in_scope | switched_off | client_cosmetic | not_needed. switched_off = a world.conf feature forced off on both sides (SPEC 'Unsupported features are world switches'); client_cosmetic = client-only presentation the GPU/RL path does not need (audio, options screens, realms, stats screens); not_needed = never reached in this game (snooper, demo mode, realms, server GUI, commands not used)
java.scope_reason: why, citing world.conf or SPEC when switched_off
java.status: exact | partial | not_ported | not_applicable. exact = every in-scope behavior has a native counterpart proven by a recording or test; partial = some members ported; not_ported = nothing native; not_applicable = scope is not in_scope

symbols: C functions, structs or tables that implement this file, each present in that file

evidence: recordings or tests that exercise it: out/java/snapshots/<name>, out/java/<area>/<name>, or csrc/tests/test_x.c; each path must exist

members.name: the member name as written in oracle/src (MCP name, or the func_/field_ SRG name where MCP left one)
members.sig: short signature, e.g. (int,int,int)V or the field type
members.native: csrc/engine/x.c:symbol where it is implemented, or null
members.note: optional: what is partial or why n/a

missing: each in-scope behavior with no native counterpart, one concrete sentence each

native.role: one or two sentences: what this file does
native.layer: tick | render | client | io | test | tool | util

java.path: oracle/src/... the vanilla file it ports
members: the Java member names it implements

structs.name: C struct or table name
structs.java: the Java class/fields it mirrors, or null

native.tick_path: bool: runs inside the server or client tick
gpu: GPU-contract hazards in this file (SPEC 'Java, then C, then the GPU'): heap allocation inside the tick, pointer graphs or linked lists, container-order dependence, recursion or unbounded loops, static or global mutable state, wall-clock or environment reads. Each: 'line N, function f: what'

oracle.role: what this harness file does (recorder, probe, replay, dev op, snapshot, ...)
oracle.kind: harness | probe | devop | snapshot | recorder | util
used_by: make targets or native tests that consume what it writes, e.g. oracle/Makefile target, csrc/tests/test_x.c
vanilla_hooks: oracle/src files that call into it

assets.path: index/assets.json (one record for the whole asset tree)

groups.name: e.g. textures/blocks, shaders/post, sounds, lang, font
native: native files that load or embed them
